text:
jess-support: @here Escalation from Acme mobile team — customer reports repeated mid-stream disconnects while streaming completions (SSE). iOS app v3.4.1, reproduces on WiFi -> cellular handoff. They see partial output then socket closed, sometimes on reconnect they get duplicate tokens billed.

jess-support: Quick repro they sent: 
```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ 
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=redwood-13b
```

jess-support: Client logs: 
```
[2025-04-03T14:12:08Z] SSE: got chunk 1024 bytes
[2025-04-03T14:12:20Z] socket closed (ECONNRESET)
[2025-04-03T14:12:20Z] retrying stream (resume=true)
[2025-04-03T14:12:20Z] billed tokens: 28.
```

jess-support: Can we triage? customer super impacted (chat UX broken). they provided request-id 86f3-req-44 and approximate client IP 34.87.12.99.

mike-plat: I can take first pass. @sara-eng can you look at whether the backend emitted [DONE] or if the LB closed the socket?

sara-eng: grabbing logs for request-id 86f3-req-44 now. initial look: server wrote several data frames, last server log shows chunked flush at 14:12:19, then connection closed by upstream at 14:12:20 with ECONNRESET from downstream. No explicit [DONE].

sara-eng: stack snippet: 
```
14:12:19.842 flush chunk (len=1024) request=86f3-req-44
14:12:19.843 write ok
14:12:20.001 tcp rst from 10.2.5.8: epoll read 0
```

dario-sre: could be idle timeout on proxy/nginx or client OS killing background sockets. What LB/proxy path for that customer? Any corp proxies in front?

jess-support: customer is on standard hosted infra region eu-west-1, no corp proxy reported. Happens when user switches from home WiFi to cellular. iOS logs show app moved to background for ~3s during handoff.

dario-sre: backgrounding + socket 3s pause + NAT rebinding commonly causes mid-stream resets. Load balancer or edge proxy may see the TCP FIN/RST and free backend connection. Also mobile carriers may NAT/port change.

mike-plat: two-pronged approach: 1) short-term workaround for client (heartbeat + smarter retry). 2) long-term: look for server-side keepalive / proxy timeout adjustments.

sara-eng: Agree. From server traces there was no server-side exception. Upstream closed by network. I recommend we advise client to emit SSE comment keepalive every ~10s: ": heartbeat\n\n" — that keeps NAT mappings alive. Also ensure they use the SDK's resumable streaming (pass conversation_id + last_token_index) so reconnects don't re-request tokens.

jess-support: customer asks about being billed twice for partial + resumed chunks. anyone confirm billing behavior?

mike-plat: Billing rules: we bill for tokens actually generated by the model. If client reconnect causes duplicate generation (resume=false), that could produce extra tokens. If resume was attempted and server deduped output, then only original tokens billed. We need to verify this request id's billing record. I'll open a billing lookup.

incident-bot: Billing lookup queued: ticket BL-779 opened for request 86f3-req-44.

sara-eng: For repro, please ask customer to run a network-handoff test with tcpdump on device (if allowed) OR we can provide a small repro app that simulates backgrounding and wifi->cell switch and the same SSE request. That will help confirm whether it's purely client side.

dario-sre: Also check edge proxy timeouts: nginx default proxy_read_timeout=60s but some infra has lower. If client sleeps > timeout, proxy may tear connection. For hosted infra we set keepalive and tcp_keepalive_time=30, but mobile NATs can still drop within 10s.

mike-plat: Proposed immediate customer guidance (send to Acme):
- Add SSE client keepalive comments every 10s.
- On reconnect, use SDK resume mode (conversation_id + last_event_index) to avoid re-requesting tokens.
- If using custom proxies, ensure proxy_read_timeout >= 90s and enable proxy_buffering off for streaming endpoints.

jess-support: I shared above to Acme and they replied: "can you provide quick code snippet for heartbeat and resume?"

sara-eng: snippet for heartbeat (js): 
```
const es = new EventSource(url, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer ...' } });
setInterval(() => {
  fetch('/sse-heartbeat', { method: 'POST', headers: {...} }); // or send comment via socket if using raw fetch
}, 10000);
```
Note: if using native EventSource you can send a lightweight xhr POST to keep NAT alive. For resume: include conversation_id in stream open and server will accept resume=true header.

mike-plat: action items: 
- sara-eng: verify server logs + confirm whether dedupe on resume worked for this request (owner: sara).
- dario-sre: validate edge proxy timeouts for eu-west-1 and propose safe defaults (owner: dario).
- mike-plat: confirm billing ticket BL-779 outcome and share whether duplicate tokens charged (owner: mike).

sara-eng: I dug into the trace: resume attempts from client included header X-Resume: true at 14:12:20 but because the original connection had no explicit end marker ([DONE]) the server treated resume as a fresh request for that conversation id and replayed tokens -> looks like dedupe logic failed when upstream close lacked finalization. Root cause: we expect generator to emit finalization event even on upstream disconnect; we didn't persist partial-output state in the resume index.

sara-eng: filing internal bug: INF-1456 — missing partial-output checkpoint write on flush. This explains duplicate generation on resume.

dario-sre: ok I'll propose config change to edge proxies to lower likelihood of mid-stream close: increase proxy_read_timeout to 120s, set tcp_keepalive_time to 20s for mobile profiles, and enable graceful socket drain on reset.

mike-plat: billing note: BL-779 shows customer was billed for both sets of tokens. We'll issue credit pending INF-1456 fix. Logged credit request CR-341.

jess-support: Customer notified and appreciates quick triage. They asked for ETA on INF-1456 and config changes.

sara-eng: INF-1456 fix: small state write on flush + resume dedupe, ETA 3 business days for canary, 7 days for full rollout.

dario-sre: proxy changes planned for next maintenance window in 48 hours; will monitor for regressions.

mike-plat: closing loop: credit CR-341 requested, testing plan for resume added to release checklist. I'll update BL-779 and mark support follow-up.

jess-support: thanks team :thumbsup: I'll keep Acme posted and attach steps and short-term client snippets.

jess-support: if anyone has other quick mitigation ideas, drop them here; otherwise I'll archive this thread once fix is deployed.
